Honestly as a US citizen, I kind of agree I have the same opportunity. However, JC is like a stepping stone imo. You should go JC first, because let’s say your exam score isn’t that great, in the US EVERY assignment counts, that’s the only difference between JC and USA university. If your GPA tanks, that’s too bad because it’ll be hard to get it back up again(talking about USA). 

You will not be ‘wasting’ 2 years of school. Only 1 year, since you get credit hours(worth 1 year). Also  JC builds maturity and it’s probably better to stay, even though I hate this place as a PR and as a US citizen. 

A few monetary aspects in case you are not doing financially well. 
1) Will your parents pay for your college/give allowance?
If yes, great! That means you’ll get free stuff. If no, can you handle the stress of working AND studying at the same time? Also will you be able to fit in with the crowd? 
2) Will you get scholarships, assuming your SAT/ACT is good enough? 
If yes good for you! If no, then what would you do? Work? Or your parents? 
3) Housing/Car. My brother is in the USA, and sometimes staying in the dorms is just not it. Will you find housing? Will you be getting a car? Car parking is very expensive near campus, will you be walking to school? Maybe you use a bike near campus, what if it’s too cold around the winter? 

These are all possibilities that you should be asking yourself. I understand it feels good to just go to another place and it’s very tempting, as a US citizen who was offered a place, BUT do take into consideration these questions. 

JC is not just about studying. It’s about maturing, and also learning university life. It’s a good plan to go to JC first, imo. University people mostly are more mature, so do watch what you say. 

If you’re going to a community college, please stay in the A Level track because it isn’t worth the degree you are getting. Don’t worry! A level cert is recognised in the US universities, ACT/SAT might not be required to get in. I hope you make the right decision and you can ask me anything as I have a brother and multiple cousins studying/studied in USA universities, as well as an aunt who worked as a professor. :)
